unresolved.finding: The Visual Studio 2010 header conflicts with the VS2008 filename and format version 10.00.
The VS2012-named solution retains the Visual Studio 2010 header and format, leaving its intended IDE association inconsistent with its filename.
The VS2017-named solution declares Visual Studio 14 and a 14.0 version, identifying the VS2015 generation instead.
The IFX solution builds the legacy test and ftnunit project files against the IFX library without establishing their compiler and module/output compatibility.
The header identifies Visual Studio version 16 while VisualStudioVersion selects version 17 for this VS2022 solution.
The IFX solution builds the legacy test and ftnunit project files against the IFX library, leaving compiler selection and module/output compatibility for the tests unclear.
The default Autoconf minimum is 2.52 although configure.ac explicitly requires at least 2.59.
The empty-minor check resets _cur_major instead of checking whether _cur_major is empty, misclassifying a major-only version.
Unquoted script and configuration paths are split on whitespace, preventing reliable operation from paths containing spaces.
The script can locate configure.ac beside itself when invoked elsewhere but still initializes and runs Autotools in the caller's working directory.
Backup creation and restoration are unchecked and the backup is deleted even after a failed restore, undermining protection against clobbering COPYING or INSTALL.
The optional download replaces executable config.guess from an unauthenticated HTTP URL without verifying its content, and curl does not reject HTTP error responses.
ret records tool availability rather than failed download status and is forced to zero after an unchecked move, so download or installation failures can escape the warning and cleanup.
libtool_failure restarts autogen with its function arguments, passing captured tool error output as command-line options instead of the original script arguments.
The second aclocal invocation saves its failure status but never checks it before continuing with configuration generation.
A missing resulting configure script produces only a warning and leaves a successful shell exit status.
Older-version branches store quotes inside devenv_path and the invocation adds another pair, producing malformed executable quoting for paths containing spaces.
Build and cleanup exit codes are checked only after type and del commands, which can replace the status and hide compilation failures.
The VS2012 branch selects Visual Studio 12.0, corresponding to VS2013 rather than VS2012's 11.0 installation.
The VS2015 environment setup uses a VC/Auxiliary/Build path and fixed Program Files location inconsistent with the selected legacy installation layout.
Unrecognized versions silently fall back to VS2008 while still constructing a solution name from that version, including the supplied newer IFX solutions.
Missing version arguments produce invalid unquoted IF comparisons rather than a controlled argument error.
The recursive deletion root comes from unchecked %1, so an omitted argument targets drive-root dist directories instead of a validated solution directory.
Directory removal failures are unchecked, allowing stale build artifacts to remain while the script proceeds.
Output directories are created only if they already existed, so this cleanup script does not initialize a fresh distribution tree.
CRLF endings break direct Unix execution and append carriage returns to the rsa key-type argument and remote hostname under Bash.
Key generation and key-copy failures are ignored and followed by success messages, with the final echo returning success.
ssh-keygen lets the user choose a key filename but ssh-copy-id always installs id_rsa.pub, potentially copying a different existing key.
CLUSTER_HOSTNAME is neither required nor quoted before constructing the remote destination.
CRLF line endings invalidate the Unix shebang and introduce literal carriage returns into Bash commands and variable values.
Failed dependency loading, configuration, compilation or installation does not prevent subsequent module publication.
Absolute /config/ is selected instead of the checkout's config directory before accessing teamcity-env.sh.
Unconditional -ffast-math allows finite-value assumptions and numerical transformations that can compromise NaN diagnostics and change scientific results.
The reused teamcity-env.sh selects gcc_12.2.0_openmpi_4.1.5_HEAD rather than the gcc_7.3.0_openmpi_4.0.4_HEAD installation created here.
chmod 777 makes the installed environment module writable by all users.
Unchecked directory changes, module loads and build commands allow packaging and module publication to proceed after failure and mask the failed build.
Installation targets /opt/xbeach but archiving reads a workspace install directory that this script neither creates nor populates.
Unconditional -ffast-math permits assumptions and arithmetic transformations that can invalidate NaN diagnostics and alter scientific results.
The module uses teamcity-env.sh even though that file selects /opt/apps and gcc_12.2.0_openmpi_4.1.5_HEAD instead of this installation's /opt/xbeach and gcc_4.9.2_1.8.3_HEAD.
The installed environment module is made world-writable with chmod 777.
Workspace and project paths use partially unquoted expansions, so whitespace in the checkout path breaks packaging or module generation.
CRLF line endings break the Unix shebang and add carriage returns to commands and variable values when the file is run through Bash.
Dependency loading and build failures do not stop installation or module generation, allowing a failed build to produce a published module.
The script changes to absolute /config/ rather than the checkout's config directory before reading teamcity-env.sh.
Unconditional -ffast-math permits finite-value assumptions and numerical transformations that can undermine NaN diagnostics and alter scientific results.
chmod 777 makes the installed shared environment module writable by every user, allowing accidental or unauthorized changes to other users' execution environment.
ERRORLEVEL is checked only after log-display commands and a second build, so the cleanup and individual build failures are not reliably preserved before tests run.
The test executable path is unquoted, so a solution directory containing spaces prevents correct execution.
Every version other than VS2010 silently selects Visual Studio 2008, including newer solution versions.
The unquoted %4 comparison becomes invalid syntax when the version argument is omitted.

The script never stops on failed directory changes, module loads, configuration, compilation or installation, allowing stale binaries to be packaged and a later successful command to mask the failed build.
Repeated cp -r into an existing _prev directory nests the current installation beneath it instead of replacing the previous snapshot.
The install staging directory is created but installation goes directly to /opt/apps, leaving the install/bin and install/lib expected by teamcity-distribute.sh unpopulated.
The scientific build unconditionally enables -ffast-math, permitting transformations and finite-value assumptions that can invalidate NaN handling and change numerical results.
Project and workspace variables are used without validation and with partially unquoted expansions, making paths containing whitespace or an empty project identifier unreliable.
Distribution targets gcc_7.3.0_1.8.3_HEAD while teamcity-env.sh selects gcc_12.2.0_openmpi_4.1.5_HEAD, so the environment does not point to this script's deployed installation.
A failed cd does not stop scp, allowing bin and lib from the previous working directory to be distributed.
Unquoted path and destination expansions and unchecked project and host variables allow whitespace or missing values to misdirect or break deployment.
The LD_LIBRARY_PATH assignment has a CRLF terminator, which adds a literal carriage return to the exported value when sourced by a Unix shell.
Appending an unset or empty LD_LIBRARY_PATH creates an empty search-path component that can include the current directory.
XBEACH_PROJECT_ID is used without validation, so an unset identifier silently selects an unintended installation path.
A stray single quote follows AC_SUBST and is emitted into configure shell code, corrupting shell quoting and preventing reliable configuration.
MPI mode and FC replacement depend on the requested option rather than an explicitly checked successful ACX_MPI result, leaving failed MPI discovery without a local failure guard.
The NetCDF fallback accepts netcdf >= 4 package metadata without checking that its Fortran module and library are present and usable by the selected compiler.
Relative configuration and output paths require the caller to be in this script's directory, but the script never establishes that working directory.
The HTML page opens even when Doxygen fails, potentially displaying stale documentation as the result of the current run.
EXCLUDE names variables.f90 relative to the invocation directory while INPUT points three levels away, so the intended source-file exclusion does not identify the file in the input directory.
Both project revision and file-version extraction are unset, leaving generated scientific code documentation without a source-version identifier.
Every formatter invocation is followed by unconditional move /Y, so a missing or failing findent can replace original sources with empty or incomplete redirected output.
Source paths are resolved from the caller's working directory without anchoring to the batch location, so launching the script elsewhere targets the wrong tree or fails.
The restart loop has no progress or failure check, so a stale ftnunit.lst combined with a launch failure or repeated crash can loop indefinitely.
The program's exit status is neither saved nor returned and subsequent logging and deletion commands can hide test execution failures from the caller.
Win32 and x64 both link mpi.lib from the same relative library directory without selecting an architecture-compatible variant.
Intermediate directories coincide with those of the colocated cxxpi project, allowing compiler and incremental-build metadata collisions.
The project named cpi builds icpi.c, leaving unclear whether the interactive variant is intentionally substituted for the named example.
Both target architectures resolve identically named MPI libraries from the same directory, so the project supplies no way to select compatible Win32 versus x64 libraries.
Intermediate directories omit the project name despite colocated example projects, leaving compiler and incremental-build files vulnerable to cross-project collisions.
Win32 and x64 link the same relative fmpich2.lib without architecture-specific library directories, leaving the x64 configurations dependent on replacing the bundled library with a compatible build.
